items.source_text: why did I receive this book ? I received this book for free, I do not know why.  I read part of it, but this is not my kind of book.  It is somewhat supernatural sleuthing, and I prefer regular police and detective books.  For the people who like scifi, this might be the thing.  But the creature presented as Angel is certainly not a witch, could be called a spirit, and there is where I stopped reading.

Just OK I have been reading all the series that his author has produced. I rotate around from one to another. Review of the trilogy I have an ebook of the trilogy.  My app shows it as 930 pages.  This first book was a solid 4 stars.  It wasn't going to be the great american novel but it was a solid read with an interesting premise and an engaging heroine.  Around page 550 is when things start to break down.  At that point I started to think the heroine just has a death wish.  She repeatedly walks into questionable situations without sufficient backup.  But it's a spy novel and some spies are adrenaline junkies so, okay.  I am now on page 800 and our character has grown less competent as the trilogy go

A writer to keep an eye on Impressive debut. It just wasn't the romance I was looking for. I stopped caring for Beth on page 196 - I wanted to take her calmly aside and say "Beth, you're 38 years old yesterday, time to grow up.". Toni I have one word for "ouch".

That being said this would be an excellent book club choice. The characters are memorable and the story moves along briskly. Having the love story told by Beth made for interesting reading.

Wendy bullies and belittles her often, but, then they wake up in each other's body and life. That means Celeste can go to work as Wendy. Or, she could pay her back by slacking off. This was a weird book I usually like Mary Kubica books. The pace of the book was so slow and when something did happen, I was scratching my head saying, "Really? That's it?" I love suspense books, when there is actually some suspense. I didn't find any in this book.  I didn't come to like any of the characters and I wished they would just grow up and go away. I didn't ponder on the book after I finished. Instead, I was glad I was done. That is 6 hours of my life I can never get back.

Poor Biscuit! Boy, it doesn't take long, does it? From new puppy to out in the dog house in just a few minutes (for me). However, being outside DOES have some advantages. For instance, how can you make a new friend if you're in the house all day with the same old friends? According to the title Biscuit has a new friend. My only suggestion would be that if someone makes a new friend, don't take him away as soon as you see him: at least give them a few minutes to play! Poor Biscuit. Get a friend, get rid of the friend. Sometimes the world needs to slow down so we can enjoy the ride!

Just Okay This book thinks it's more clever than it is. Written to be a psychological thriller in the vein of Gone Girl, it fails to hold the tension of that work.
